local_supplier.title: Restriction of the regular representation to a closed subgroup
local_supplier.statement: Assume AC. If $G$ is a locally compact Hausdorff group and $H\leq G$ is closed, then $\lambda_G|_H\prec\lambda_H$, where the left regular representations use fixed left Haar measures and weak containment has the finite-sum diagonal-coefficient meaning of [[def-weak-containment-of-unitary-representations]].
local_supplier.strategy: Write r for the rho-function and R_H for the right regular representation. Obtain r and the Radon measure mu on X=G/H from [[thm-existence-of-rho-functions-and-quasi-invariant-measures-on-g-mod-h]] and [[thm-weil-quotient-integration-formula-with-rho-function]]. Fix f in C_c(G), S=supp(f), and put a_x(h)=[Delta_G((xh)^(-1))/r(xh)]^(1/2) f((xh)^(-1)). Its support is contained in x^(-1)S^(-1) intersect H, hence compact. Inversion and the Weil formula, applied to the continuous compactly supported integrand Delta_G(y^(-1)) f((yk)^(-1)) overline(f(y^(-1)))/r(y), yield c_f(k)=<lambda_G(k)f,f>=integral_X B(q,k)dmu(q), where B(xH,k)=<R_H(k)a_x,a_x>. Indeed r(xhk)/r(xh)=Delta_H(k)/Delta_G(k), so the square-root factors give precisely Delta_H(k)^(1/2) a_x(hk) overline(a_x(h)). For t in H, a_(xt)(h)=a_x(th); left Haar invariance therefore makes B independent of the representative x. The integrand is continuous in (x,k,h); on compact x-neighborhoods its h-support is confined to C^(-1)S^(-1) intersect H because of its second factor. Compact-kernel continuity gives continuity in (x,k), and openness of the quotient map gives a continuous function B on X times H. B vanishes off the compact T=p(S^(-1)), independently of k. For any compact Q in H, q->B(q,.)|Q is continuous into C(Q) in its sup norm (use a finite subcover of Q for joint continuity). Cover T by finitely many neighborhoods on which this map oscillates by less than delta, take the resulting disjoint Borel partition E_j of T, pick q_j in each nonempty E_j, and lift q_j to x_j. Radon compact finiteness gives mu(T)<infinity, and sup_Q|integral_T B(q,k)dmu - sum_j mu(E_j)B(q_j,k)| <= delta mu(T). If mu(T)=0 use the zero coefficient; otherwise choose delta so this is below the desired tolerance. The sum consists of right-regular diagonal coefficients at eta_j=sqrt(mu(E_j))a_(x_j). Convert them to left-regular coefficients locally: Jb(h)=Delta_H(h)^(-1/2)b(h^(-1)) is an isometry on C_c(H) by [[lem-haar-change-of-variables-under-inversion]], satisfies J^2=I and J lambda_H(k)=R_H(k)J, and extends unitarily by [[lem-complex-haar-l1-and-l2-are-complete-and-cc-dense]]. Thus use J eta_j for lambda_H. Finally approximate any xi in L2(G) by f in C_c(G); unitarity and Cauchy-Schwarz give sup_(k in H)|c_xi(k)-c_f(k)| <= (||xi||_2+||f||_2)||xi-f||_2. This proves the exact finite-sum coefficient definition [[def-weak-containment-of-unitary-representations]]. All choices and supplier choice hypotheses are covered by AC; no measurable section, countability, direct integral, or global sigma-finite product theorem is used.

def-left-uniformly-continuous-bounded-fu.statement: Let G be an LCH group with fixed left Haar measure. Define UCB(G) to be the space of actual bounded complex functions phi:G->C for which ||L_x phi-phi||_sup->0 as x->e, where (L_x phi)(y)=phi(x^(-1)y). These functions are continuous, form a closed translation-invariant subspace of the bounded functions with the sup norm, and the translation action is jointly continuous. Haar full support implies ||phi||_sup=||[phi]||_Linf, so phi->[phi] embeds UCB(G) isometrically into L-infinity(G); in particular a UCB function that vanishes almost everywhere vanishes everywhere.
def-left-uniformly-continuous-bounded-fu.strategy: Pointwise continuity: for fixed t, phi(yt)-phi(t) is bounded in absolute value by ||L_(y^(-1))phi-phi||_sup, which tends to zero as y->e; since y->yt is a homeomorphism, phi is continuous at t. Every nonempty open set has positive Haar measure, so continuity gives sup=essential sup and injectivity. Closedness follows from the epsilon/3 argument. Translation invariance follows from L_x L_g=L_g L_(g^(-1)xg) and continuity of conjugation. Joint continuity follows from ||L_x phi-L_(x0)phi0||_sup <= ||phi-phi0||_sup+||L_(x0^(-1)x)phi0-phi0||_sup. This uses actual functions throughout and does not assert pointwise properties of arbitrary representatives of an L-infinity class.
def-left-uniformly-continuous-bounded-fu.reason: Replace illegitimate pointwise use of arbitrary Linfinity representatives with the source pointwise UCB definition and its isometric embedding.

lem-l1-convolution-with-an-l-infinity-fu.statement: Assume AC. For f in L1(G) and phi in L-infinity(G), convolution (f*phi)(x)=integral_G f(y)phi(y^(-1)x)dmu(y) defines a bounded actual function, independent of the chosen representatives, with ||f*phi||_sup <= ||f||_1||phi||_infinity. It lies in UCB(G), and ||L_g(f*phi)-f*phi||_sup <= ||L_g f-f||_1||phi||_infinity. Convolution is bilinear, L_g(f*phi)=(L_g f)*phi, and for f,b in L1(G) one has (f*b)*phi=f*(b*phi).
lem-l1-convolution-with-an-l-infinity-fu.strategy: Take a bounded Borel representative of phi. For each fixed x, y->y^(-1)x sends Haar null sets to Haar null sets by inversion and translation, so its convolution value is representative independent; changing f on a null set is also harmless. The pointwise absolute integral is bounded by ||f||_1||phi||_infinity. Left invariance, using y=gz, gives L_g(f*phi)=(L_g f)*phi; hence its sup-norm defect is bounded by ||L_g f-f||_1||phi||_infinity. Strong L1 translation continuity proves the pointwise UCB condition and therefore continuity/measurability. Associativity follows first for compactly supported f,b by an absolutely integrable two-variable Fubini calculation (the phi representative is bounded and x fixed), followed by L1 approximation and the sup-norm bound. For general f,b the needed double integral can equally be confined, modulo null sets, to sigma-compact supports supplied by countably many Cc approximations; Haar is sigma-finite there. Do not claim f*(L_g phi)=L_g(f*phi): this fails in general for nonabelian G.
lem-l1-convolution-with-an-l-infinity-fu.reason: Remove false nonabelian translation identity; supply actual continuous convolution function and associativity needed by its consumer.

lem-a-ucb-invariant-mean-yields-a-topolo.strategy: For probability f in L1 and psi in UCB, first prove m(f*psi)=m(psi). On a compact K carrying all but arbitrarily small f-mass, norm-continuity of y->L_y psi supplies a finite Borel partition with uniformly small oscillation. The weighted finite sum sum_j (integral_(E_j) f)dmu L_(y_j)psi approximates integral_K f(y)L_y psi dmu in sup norm. Its m-value is m(psi) integral_K f. The tail has norm bounded by ||psi||_sup integral_(G minus K) f. Such K exist by Cc density (or finite Radon inner regularity). Passing to arbitrarily small errors proves the identity without invoking Bochner measurability on a non-sigma-compact domain. Let e_U be the published positive probability approximate-identity net. Applying the identity with psi=e_U*phi gives m((f*e_U)*phi)=m(e_U*phi). The correct convergence estimate is ||(f*e_U)*phi-f*phi||_sup <= ||f*e_U-f||_1||phi||_infinity->0. Thus m(f*phi)=lim_U m(e_U*phi), independent of probability f. Positivity and unitality of m-tilde(phi)=m(f0*phi) are immediate. Associativity and independence of the probability kernel yield m-tilde(f*phi)=m((f0*f)*phi)=m(f0*phi)=m-tilde(phi). No assertion of sup-norm approximate-identity convergence for arbitrary L-infinity phi is used.
lem-a-ucb-invariant-mean-yields-a-topolo.reason: Replace false Linfinity sup convergence with the valid right L1 approximate-identity estimate and finite-partition integration.

thm-amenability-is-stable-under-closed-s.statement: Assume AC. Let $G$ be a locally compact Hausdorff group. (i) If $G$ is amenable, every closed subgroup $H\leq G$ is amenable. (ii) If $G$ is amenable and $N\trianglelefteq G$ is closed normal, the Hausdorff quotient $G/N$ is amenable. (iii) If $N\trianglelefteq G$ is closed normal and both $N$ and $G/N$ are amenable, then $G$ is amenable.
thm-amenability-is-stable-under-closed-s.strategy: Use the repaired pointwise UCB(G), identified isometrically with its L-infinity subspace. An invariant mean on L-infinity restricts to UCB; conversely the local invariant-mean-to-Reiter and Reiter-to-mean lemmas give amenability from an invariant UCB mean, with all AC assumptions carried. (i) By [[thm-hulanicki-weak-containment-criterion-for-amenability]], amenability gives 1_G prec lambda_G. Every compact subset Q of closed H is compact in G, so restriction of the coefficient approximations gives 1_H prec lambda_G|H. The new [[lem-restricted-regular-representation-is-weakly-contained-in-subgroup-regular-representation]] and transitivity proved in [[def-weak-containment-of-unitary-representations]] give 1_H prec lambda_H. Apply the same Hulanicki theorem to the LCH group H. (ii) If pi:G->G/N is the open quotient map, pullback is an isometric positive unital embedding UCB(G/N)->UCB(G), and L_g(psi o pi)=(L_(gN)psi) o pi. Restrict the G-invariant mean along it to obtain a G/N-invariant UCB mean, hence amenability. (iii) For phi in UCB(G) set phi_g(h)=phi(gh) on N and F_phi(g)=m_N(phi_g). For fixed g, ||L_n phi_g-phi_g||_sup <= ||L_(gng^(-1))phi-phi||_sup->0 as n->e in N. Thus phi_g is in UCB(N); the conjugation must be included. Invariance of m_N gives F_phi(gn)=F_phi(g), since phi_(gn)(h)=phi_g(nh)=L_(n^(-1))phi_g(h). Moreover ||L_gamma F_phi-F_phi||_sup <= ||L_gamma phi-phi||_sup->0, so F_phi is continuous and UCB on G and descends through the open pi to psi_phi on G/N. To prove quotient UCB, for any small-error identity neighborhood V of G its image pi(V) is an identity neighborhood of G/N, and each coset in pi(V) has a representative gamma in V; the same bound then holds for L_(gamma N)psi_phi-psi_phi uniformly. Define m(phi)=m_(G/N)(psi_phi). Linearity, positivity and m(1)=1 follow from those of the two means. F_(L_gamma phi)=L_gamma F_phi implies psi_(L_gamma phi)=L_(gamma N)psi_phi, hence m is G-invariant and G is amenable. This proves all clauses in full LCH generality with nets.

thm-amenability-is-stable-under-closed-s.reason: Close closed-subgroup proof, remove vacuous opening amenability premise for the extension clause, and correct conjugation in UCB(N) restriction.
